main_body: Round stone well base (rows 14-31) under a thin wooden crossbeam frame with posts, rope and bucket
top_band: Light grey-green stone rim, rows 14-17 at the back, curving around a dark water opening (rows 17-21), then a lighter front rim at rows 21-22
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the pale back rim is followed by a dark blue water ellipse with a highlight, then a light front rim line, then a darker band under the rim. Below that is the stone front face with block shading down to row 31. The opening is a visible ellipse with water inside and the rim is several rows thick, so the stone body reads as a proper 3/4 container. The front blocks are only shaded and not truly inset, which is a minor weakness.

style.evidence: The stone ramp has about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) and the water has 2-3 blues. Outlines are a tinted dark grey-green, not black. The wooden beam and posts are shallow, with 2-3 flat orange tones and no grain, and the beam is a large flat band. The reference well has a tiled roof with scallops and per-tile highlights, plus more textured stones, so the candidate looks thinner and flatter next to it. Its front stone blocks also have little speckle.
